With excellent typing, Supreme Overlord, and Sucker Punch, Kingambit is a premier revenge killer that can also check Mega Gengar lacking Focus Blast. Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave: Sucker Punch helps pick off weakened attackers and is excellent insurance against late-game Choice Scarf users like Basculegion-M and Garchomp. Kowtow Cleave is usually needed as a second Dark-type attack, though, particularly for targets like Substitute Mega Gengar that can play around Sucker Punch. Swords Dance: Kingambit's amazing bulk allows it to consistently survive big hits such as Jolly Garchomp's Earthquake, letting it set up a Swords Dance and fire back with +2 Sucker Punch. Iron Head versus Low Kick: Iron Head provides the best all-around power and coverage, allowing Kingambit to better threaten Primarina, Mimikyu, and Mega Floette. Low Kick is less flexible and leaves Kingambit vulnerable to Primarina, but it's the best way to take on opposing Kingambit and has a high chance to OHKO offensive Hydreigon after Stealth Rock damage. Items Black Glasses: Black Glasses doubles down on making Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave as deadly as possible. When combined with Supreme Overlord, +2 Sucker Punch + Black Glasses will always OHKO offensive Garchomp. Chople Berry: Chople Berry allows Kingambit to withstand some weaker Fighting-type attacks, such as Close Combat from Aegislash and Scizor and unboosted Body Press from Corviknight. With maximum HP investment, Kingambit also has a high chance to survive Jolly Mega Lopunny's Close Combat and an average chance to survive Timid Mega Gengar's Focus Blast.

Speed SP Benchmarks While Kingambit normally doesn't focus on Speed, moving first means Kingambit can improve certain matchups like Primarina. Generally speaking, it is recommended to sacrifice HP instead of Attack if wanting to reallocate to Speed. Versus Aegislash: Keep in mind that outrunning Aegislash potentially means dealing reduced damage while it's in Shield forme. If Kingambit is running Chople Berry to withstand Sacred Sword or Close Combat, letting Aegislash attack and switch formes essentially guarantees that a healthy Kingambit can OHKO afterwards. 3 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed negative Speed nature Aegislash. 11 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested base 60 Speed targets such as Clefable before Mega Evolution, Primarina, and Aegislash. 12 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Tyranitar. 16 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Scizor before Mega Evolution. 18 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Corviknight, though its superior bulk and access to Body Press mean that it is still overwhelmingly favored in the matchup. 21 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Mega Clefable, though keep in mind that Mega Clefable often receives Speed boosts from Baton Pass Espathra. 26 Speed: This allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Mega Scizor.

Basculgion-M is enjoying a fantastic offensive type combination in the current metagame, which, when combined with Adaptability, makes it a standout pick as a late-game sweeper with Last Respects and a potent early-game scout with Flip Turn. Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf gives Basculegion-M the Speed it needs to chunk foes and get out safely early-game while also allowing you to bring it in late-game without spending a turn to set up Agility. However, Basculegion-M's pitiful base 78 Speed means that it will be outsped by most of the other Choice Scarf users in the format, as well as most Dragon Dance users, so you need to be careful when positioning Basculegion-M. Wave Crash: Wave Crash will be Basculegion-M's primary early-game damage option if you elect to not pivot it out. Last Respects: Even after just one team member is KOed, Last Respects becomes an extremely potent move that's very difficult to switch into, and it gives Basculegion-M immense sweeping power once both allies have fainted. Flip Turn: Adaptability allows Flip Turn to deal notable damage for a pivoting move. Aqua Jet: Adaptability-boosted Aqua Jet does a considerable amount of damage and can get Basculegion-M out of trouble against other priority users or Speed-boosted foes. Other Options Ice Fang: Ice Fang provides coverage against Dragon-types and threatens Garchomp and Dragonite right out of the gate. Head Smash: Head Smash gives Basculegion-M a heavily damaging coverage option that threatens Gyarados and Dragonite.

This Agility set gives Basculegion-M the freedom to outspeed and threaten the majority of its metagame-relevant foes while enabling it to use multiple moves. Opposing Priority Users: While setting up Agility can make Basculegion-M an absolutely terrifying sweeper, late-game checks such as Aegislash, Mimikyu, and Kingambit are quite popular in the current metagame, so be careful when you see these during Team Preview. Adamant Nature: Agility's boost is going to give Basculegion-M plenty of Speed to set up its sweep. As Basculegion-M lacks an Attack-boosting setup move, an Adamant nature is preferred over Jolly. Adamant Basculegion-M is already outspeeding Choice Scarf Garchomp with an Agility boost, while a Jolly nature won't allow it to outspeed the likes of Choice Scarf Jolly Meowscarada. Items Mystic Water versus Spell Tag: These items will allow Basculegion-M's STAB moves to do hilariously high damage. Mystic Water allows Basculegion-M to OHKO physically defensive Hippowdon with Wave Crash and has the added bonus of juicing up Aqua Jet's damage when it needs to rely on priority. On the other hand, Spell Tag will allow Last Respects to tear through walls, letting it OHKO maximum HP Mega Scizor after Stealth Rock at 150 Base Power. Focus Sash: Focus Sash ensures that Basculegion-M is going to tank a hit while it sets up Agility, but because entry hazards are very popular in the current metagame, saving your Focus Sash user for last can be a risky venture.

With the powerful Unburden ability, Sneasler can become a dangerous cleaner that wrecks havoc on frailer teams. Throat Chop versus Shadow Claw : When covering Psychic- and Ghost-types, Throat Chop is usually preferred for its higher power over Shadow Claw. However, Adamant Sneasler with Shadow Claw has about a 50/50 chance to knock out offensive Mimikyu after Disguise breaks. Swords Dance : If allowed to set up a Swords Dance, Sneasler can quickly spiral out of control and even overpower Hippowdon and Corviknight if they have been chipped. Fake Out: Fake Out can help get targets into KO range of its more powerful attacks, and the priority helps Sneasler catch faster foes prior to activating Unburden. Adamant versus Jolly: Adamant is usually preferred to maximize sweeping potential, and with Unburden active, Sneasler can effortlessly outrun even Choice Scarf Dragapult. WIth maximum investment, Adamant Sneasler also maintains enough Speed to outrun threats like Mega Glimmora and unboosted Garchomp before Unburden's boost. Jolly gives Sneasler a little more consistency, allowing it to outrun more threats such as Mega Starmie and Focus Sash Gengar before Unburden activates. Other Options Acrobatics: Acrobatics is Sneasler's best move against threats like Mega Venusaur, Volcarona, and opposing Sneasler, though the move's damage is reliant on Sneasler consuming its item beforehand. Rock Slide: Rock Slide landing a clean OHKO on Mega Charizard Y is huge, but its uses are otherwise limited. Fling: Fling with King's Rock or Light Ball is the most flexible method of triggering Sneasler's Unburden, but the sacrifice to damage and coverage makes it a hard sell. Items White Herb: White Herb synergizes fantastically with Sneasler, allowing it to activate Unburden through its best attack Close Combat while also nullifying the defense drops once. White Herb can also function as insurance against Intimidate users. Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry can give the somewhat frail Sneasler a bit more survivability, especially against priority attacks. However, it does make Sneasler reliant on the opponent to trigger Unburden for it. Lum Berry: Lum Berry puts Sneasler into a more niche role for its team, focused on countering status users like Yawn Umbreon and Will-O-Wisp Rotom-Wash.

Archaludon is one of the best walls in the entire game thanks to its incredible bulk and Stamina. With access to Stealth Rock, phazing support, and Draco Meteor, Archaludon can efficiently wear down lineups that lack dedicated checks to it. Thunderbolt versus Flash Cannon: Thunderbolt is Archaludon's best complementary move to Draco Meteor for its ability to hit key bulky targets Primarina and Corviknight, which comfortably check Archaludon otherwise, as well as hitting many other Steel-types neutrally. Flash Cannon is a more consistent damage source overall, but it doesn't help Archaludon against Steel-types like Corviknight, Scizor, and Aegislash. Roar versus Dragon Tail: Roar is the preferred phazing option for racking up Stealth Rock damage, as Pokemon immune to it are extremely uncommon, and it works through Substitute. Dragon Tail is more generally oppressive by dealing direct damage and phazing at the same time, and it additionally cannot be shut down by Taunt. However, Dragon Tail can make Archaludon struggle against Substitute users and does not work at all on Mega Floette, which can set up on Archaludon and threaten to snowball out of control. Mirror Coat: Archaludon's bulk makes it a viable user of Mirror Coat, which allows it to deal significant damage or completely take out targets such as Primarina and Mega Gengar. Sitrus Berry versus Leftovers: Sitrus Berry's burst recovery is more effective at helping Archaludon survive multiple hits from big attacks, including super effective ones like Garchomp's Earthquake. On the other hand, Leftovers is superior when Archaludon can capitalize long-term on Stamina boosts from favorable defensive matchups against foes such as Meowscarada and Mega Starmie. Other Options Foul Play: Foul Play gives Archaludon a direct option against difficult physical attackers like Aegislash and Scizor, especially if they try to set up with Swords Dance. Rest and Chesto Berry: Restoring Archaludon to full health after receiving several Stamina boosts can completely ruin physically offensive lineups that rely on attrition to beat Archaludon. Iron Head: Specially defensive Archaludon with Iron Head is a specific adaptation to check Calm Mind Floette. If going this route, Archaludon generally should run a Careful nature over Calm and Dragon Tail over Draco Meteor. SP Spreads All 2HKOs mentioned below factor in Archaludon having a +1 Defense boost from Stamina for the second hit. 32 HP / 23 Def / 11 SpD with Bold: With this spread, Archaludon is guaranteed to avoid the 2HKO from Jolly Basculegion-M's 150-Base Power Last Respects and, when using Sitrus Berry, Adamant Garchomp's Earthquake. Leftover SPs are put into Special Defense. 32 HP / 2 Def / 32 SpD with Calm: Maximum special bulk investment allows Archaludon to avoid the 2HKO from Timid Mega Gengar's Shadow Ball and Modest Primarina's Moonblast, assuming no Fairy Feather on the latter. This spread works particularly well with Mirror Coat, as Archaludon also has a significant chance to survive +1 Moonblast from offensive Mega Floette.

Archaludon can perform consistently as an offensive lead thanks to Sturdy, which lets it take full advantage of its respectable Speed and high-power attacks. Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt provides strong overlapping coverage with Draco Meteor, in particular pressuring defensive mainstays Primarina and Corviknight. Flash Cannon versus Steel Beam: Flash Cannon is the safest option for a Steel-type STAB attack and is more than sufficient against the likes of offensive Mimikyu and Glimmora. However, Steel Beam's massive Base Power makes dealing with bulkier threats like Hippowdon and defensive Mega Floette much more viable, even if it comes at the cost of survivability. Aura Sphere: Aura Sphere helps Archaludon win the mirror matchup while avoiding Draco Meteor usage, keeping its Special Attack stable and making it less likely to become setup bait. Even specially defensive Archaludon has a high chance to be 2HKOed. Aura Sphere is also the best option for taking on Kingambit. Stealth Rock: The combination of Archaludon's Speed and Sturdy allows it to reliably set Stealth Rock. Roar: Roar can disrupt dangerous setup sweepers like Calm Mind Mega Floette and Swords Dance Mega Lucario. Timid versus Modest: Many offensive threats such as Adamant Mimikyu, Jolly Basculegion-M, Jolly Hisuian Samurott, and Jolly Mega Gyarados are at or just below Archaludon's positive-nature Speed tier. As such, a Timid nature is usually preferred. However, the power increase from a Modest nature is still worth considering; for example, it gives Archaludon a decent chance to OHKO offensive Mega Gengar with Draco Meteor. Other Options Dark Pulse: Dark Pulse is offensive Archaludon's best means of pressuring Aegislash directly. Mirror Coat: Sturdy allows for more confident Mirror Coat usage, especially against targets like Mega Floette that boost their Special Attack, but it limits the direct offensive nature that this set likes to utilize and is very reliant on Sturdy being active. Items White Herb: White Herb allows Archaludon to fire off Draco Meteor once without worrying about the subsequent Special Attack drop, giving it incredible burst potential and generally making it less exploitable by setup attackers. Sitrus Berry: Archaludon's defensive typing and stats are so strong naturally that Sitrus Berry can still be worth running on an offensive set. Sitrus Berry will also always activate after using Steel Beam, giving Archaludon an extra health buffer as well as the potential to fire off a second Steel Beam without fainting.

When paired with a rain setter like Pelipper, Archaludon can build dangerous offensive momentum with Electro Shot. Electro Shot : Thanks to the Special Attack boost, even the first Electro Shot used can be difficult to switch into without an Electric resistance, and it can also OHKO frailer targets like Mega Lucario. Draco Meteor : Electro Shot may be the star of the show, but Draco Meteor is often Archaludon's best option when you're trying to play around Ground-type switch-ins such as Garchomp. Aura Sphere: Aura Sphere provides consistent coverage independent from the weather, pressuring Dark-types like Kingambit and opposing Archaludon. Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt is an alternative Electric-type option to use outside of rain, which can be especially relevant for keeping pressure on Mega Charizard Y. SP Spreads and Items 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe with Timid: A standard offensive spread for use with Choice Scarf. A Timid nature is mandatory, as Archaludon wants to outrun Choice Scarf Jolly Basculegion-M. 32 HP / 11 Def / 15 SpA / 8 Spe with Modest: Going with a bulkier spread along with a Sitrus Berry sacrifices immediate offensive pressure, but it eases the need for prediction and allows Archaludon more flexibility in and out of rain. Enough Special Attack investment is maintained to guarantee that Electro Shot OHKOes offensive Mega Gyarados, and the Speed investment is enough to outrun fully invested base 60s like Primarina. The remaining SPs go into HP and Defense, giving Archaludon a decent chance of avoiding the 2HKO from Jolly Garchomp's Earthquake after Sitrus Berry healing and a Stamina activiation.
